key_insight: GaOx can act as a conductive hole transport layer for 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells when formed in the right growth conditions, enabling strong passivation and high voltage without extra Cu, Na, Ag, or heavy alkalis.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical back-contact/passivation strategy for tandem-ready chalcopyrite bottom cells, helping push CuInSe2 devices toward higher efficiency and VOC targets.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap CuInSe2 absorber via ion exchange.
Compared the need for additional Cu, Na, and sputtering oxygen flow to test what makes GaOx conductive.
Characterized the resulting layer as partly crystalline and evaluated finished solar-cell performance.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved above 16% active-area efficiency and a record-certified VOC of 552 mV for a 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cell.
watch_item: The conductive GaOx behavior appears sensitive to formation conditions, so replication may require tight control of growth and interface processing.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
